pages.confirms: Lettre CCCLXXXV opening ('LETTRE CCCLXXXV. Le Prince d'Orange au Comte Jean de Nassau. Details de son expedition'), matches ciphertext.txt lines 1-40; no cipher numerals on this page

the cipher-numeral runs and the editor's footnote (1), printed clearly and legibly as groups of 1-2 digit Arabic numerals separated by periods, e.g. '24. 31. 48. 60. 15. 33. 54. 9. 42. 60. 45. 25. d. e. 35. 36. 3. 54. s. 61. 60. 15. 13.'; the cached OCR's 'i5'/'6o'/'3i' etc. are OCR misreadings of clearly-printed '15'/'60'/'31' -- not print artefacts. Footnote reads (transcribed from the image): 'Il est a regretter qu'une comparaison attentive des passages suivants avec d'autres pieces dont nous possedons le dechiffrement, n'ait conduit a aucun resultat. On s'est convaincu que les chiffres y etant infiniment plus nombreux que les lettres, il sera tres difficile, si non decidement impossible, de retrouver le sens.' -- the OCR's version of this footnote (ciphertext.txt) has several word-level garbles ('raimnts' for 'suivants', 'decbiiTremeQt' for 'dechiffrement') but is otherwise faithful

further cipher-numeral runs continue on this page (confirms the letter's ciphertext is not confined to p.502-503; it recurs through at least p.509 per the OCR text), matches ciphertext.txt; also confirms the massacre/campaign narrative (Coligny/Rochefoucault/Teligny, Dendremonde) reads in clear prose around the cipher runs, as in the OCR
